text: The blood work shows normal inflammation markers and no infection, which is good news. Given your family history and the isolated nature of the swelling, does the pain feel better when you rest and worse when you move or put weight on the knee?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Idiopathic Transient Synovitis.

I have reviewed your medical history and lab results; given the age, lack of fever, normal inflammatory markers, and the self-limiting nature of the swelling in a young child, this is the most likely diagnosis. Please ensure your son can bear weight and that we monitor for any return of high fever or inability to walk.
